articleTitle: Mathematical Model of Electromagnetic Field Influence on Plant Environment with Insect Pests
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The paper examines a mathematical model of the influence of the electromagnetic field on the plant environment with insect pests, namely the interaction of radio pulses with the layer of the plant environment and the calculation of the average electromagnetic field in the plant layer. The dependence of the normalized value of the average electric field on the filling frequency of the radio pulse, the biotropic parameters of the electromagnetic field for the destruction of insect pests of agricultural crops are given.

articleTitle: Study of Energy Density as a Measure of the Impact of Electromagnetic Radiation on Biological Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The article is devoted to the study of energy density as a standardized indicator for assessing the effectiveness of medical personnel protective systems against microwave radiation. The key feature of the proposed method is the ability to translate measurements of complex fields into equivalent values of the energy density of a plane wave, which allows them to be compared with existing measurements of power density. The results can be used in practice in conditions where it is necessary to assess the impact of electromagnetic radiation on medical personnel and the need to develop protective measures.

articleTitle: Study of a Pulsed Radio Source of Radiation in the Centimeter Range for the Destruction of Insect Pests of Agricultural Crops
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The work examines a radio pulse source of centimeter wave radiation for the destruction of agricultural pests, namely the reliability of theoretical approaches and models based on the development and research of the main characteristics of a synchronizing generator, prototyping and debugging of electronic systems of a 12-diode generator for the destruction of agricultural pests. The dependence of the frequency stretching band on the coupling coefficient between the resonators and the dependence of the pulse power of a twelve-diode generator on the duty cycle of the pulses are given.

articleTitle: Application of the Hall Effect to Excite Electric Current in a Biological Substance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: An overview of the use of the Hall effect in solids is presented, the quantum Hall effect is described, as well as the Hall effect in electrolytes. The possibility of using the Hall effect to excite electric current in a biological substance is being considered with the prospect of using it in medicine for diagnostic and therapeutic purposes.

articleTitle: Compensation of the Electrodes Skewing Error of Runout Capacitive Sensors for Hydro Generators Condition Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: In the paper presents a method for reducing the error of capacitive runout sensors, which arises due to the non-parallelism (skew) of the flat electrodes of the sensor relative to the measurement surface. The ratios of the sizes of the external and internal electrodes have been found, at which the main component of the transformation error “microdisplacement - reciprocal value of capacitance” tend towards an infinitesimal value. The effectiveness of the proposed correction method is analyzed depending on the electrode skew coefficient. It is shown that the relative measurement error at large skew angles decreases several times, and at small ones - several hundred times.

articleTitle: Analysis of Human Body Vibrations in the Frequency Domain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The authors developed an experimental setup and conducted studies of the distribution of physical loads in the patient's foot, on the basis of which a model was developed for calculating vibrations acting on the human body. This information allows improving the quality of diagnostics of patients with lower limb injuries during their treatment and rehabilitation.

articleTitle: Initial Dynamic Characteristics of the Processes Under Magnetic-Pulsed Transportation of the Conductor in the Guiding Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The proposed work was initiated by the needs of modern industry in new efficient technologies based on the use of the energy of electromagnetic fields. The purpose of the work is to determine the characteristics of the initial dynamics of the directed movement of a conducting object under the action of the forces of a high-frequency magnetic field generated by an inductor in the cavity of a structure concentrating the excited pressure in a fixed direction, and to numerically estimate the initial velocities of the object of force action in the absence and presence of resistance forces of various physical nature. The dynamics of the movement of a conductor under a force magnetic-impulse effect in the presence and absence of resistance forces from the external environment is theoretically investigated as novelty. Main results. It is shown that, for any resistance, the characteristic time of velocity rise in the field of magnetic pressure forces does not exceed ~60 µs, A significant and decisive influence of aerodynamic drag forces on the velocity characteristics of the movement of an object of force action is shown. So, already at ~100 µs, the speed drops by more than two times. Practical significance. Calculations illustrating dynamic processes under magnetic-pulse force action on conductive objects in the experimental equipment of the Kharkiv National Automobile and Highway University have been performed. Estimates of the dynamics under the maximum possible action of resistance forces make it possible to give recommendations on the formation of optimal high-speed modes of motion of conducting objects under the force action of pulsed magnetic fields.

articleTitle: Detection Computer Network Intrusion Using Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: In this work, the effectiveness of using classical machine learning methods and modern deep neural network models for intrusion detection in computer networks has been investigated. The purpose of this work is to develop a model for detecting intrusions into computer networks based on the Transformer model using tabular input data. In this work, the UNSW-NB15 dataset is used as the source data. This dataset contains information about normal network behaviour as well as during synthetic intrusions. Models for intrusion detection in computer networks based on machine learning methods were investigated: Decision Tree, KNN, Logistic Regression, SVM, Gradient Boosting, Random Forest. A method of converting tabular data into images was developed, which made it possible to build intrusion detection models based on Vision Transformer and Vision Transformer for small-size datasets on modern Transformer architecture. The research results showed that developed model based on Vision Transformer and Vision Transformer for small-size datasets improves the quality of identification, and eliminates the need for a preprocessing step such as dimensionality reduction.

articleTitle: Propagation of Terahertz Laser Vortex Beams from a Metal Waveguide Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The purpose of this work is to obtain analytical expressions describing the nonparaxial diffraction of wave modes of the metal waveguide resonator of a terahertz laser during the wave mode interaction with a spiral phase plate. The Rayleigh-Sommerfeld vector theory is adopted to consider the propagation of vortex laser beams generated by wave modes of the quasi-optical waveguide cavity when interacting with a spiral phase plate in different diffraction zones. The resulting vortex beams are examined for their physical features in free space propagation.

articleTitle: Infrared H-polarized Plane Wave Scattering by Dielectric Cylinder with Coplanar Graphene Strips
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The scattering and absorption of the H-polarized plane wave by a system of coplanar graphene strips inside a dielectric cylinder is considered in the infrared frequency range. We employ a mathematically grounded approach based on the Green's function and hyper-singular integral equations, which are discretized using the meshless Nystrom-type algorithm. Due to the strong dependence of graphene conductivity on the chemical potential, RCS of the structure can be tuned over a wide range, making it greater or smaller than that of the cylinder without the strips. This tunability is especially pronounced near the frequencies of the first plasmon resonance.

articleTitle: The Effect of the Design Paddle Electrothermomechanical System on Duration of Heating Substance in the Biogas Reactor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: For rational use organic raw materials, it is necessary to create microclimate parameters in biogas reactors that correspond to conditions anaerobic fermentation. The creation of these parameters and the selection of the necessary equipment for this is a complex and important issue from the point of view of saving electricity and increasing the interest investors in introduction of biogas production. Purpose of study was to investigate influence of positional law of changes in applied power to the heating device of an electrothermo mechanical system with different paddle designs. The electrothermomechanical system includes paddles with surface-mounted electric heaters protected by a steel casing. In the research, paddles of two designs were used, namely: steel monolithic and steel hollow paddles, the cavity of which is filled with a filler (wax). To achieve goal, mathematical model was built using differential equations. Numerical calculations were performed in the Wolfram Mathematica application program. The power applied to the electric heater changed according to the positional law. The result of the conducted research was obtaining graphic dependences temperature change of substance using monolithic and wax-filled paddles. It is established that electric heating of volume <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.04}\ \mathbf{m}^{\mathbf{3}}$</tex> of matter from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{34}\ {}^{\circ}\mathbf{C}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{35.8}\ {}^{\circ}\mathbf{C}$</tex> using paddles whose cavity is filled with wax occurs faster by 8.2% on average. The average rate of increase in temperature substance in first 100 seconds of heater operation is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.0008}\ {}^{\circ}\mathbf{C}/\mathbf{s}$</tex>, which is 56% more than the average rate of increase in temperature when using monolithic steel paddles. The conducted research made it possible to establish that average value temperature of spiral heating cable placed on paddle with filler (wax) is on average 4.6% higher compared to temperature spiral of heating device placed on monolithic steel paddle. Provided it is placed in a biogas reservoir (reactor) with a volume of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.04}\ \mathbf{m}^{\mathbf{3}}$</tex>. In work shows a graphical dependence and established for the first time that in the first 200 seconds of operation the heating device, change in temperature filler (wax) occurs according to a parabolic law. The obtained positive results can be used in investigation and creation systems for automatic control of heating devices in reactors, which will allow create energy-efficient systems and increase profitability of processes of heating substances in reactors.

articleTitle: Improving the Electrical Resistivity of Blast-Fumace Coke
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The influence of the addition of petroleum coke on the quality of coal charges and blast furnace coke obtained from them has been determined. Four variants of coal charges with different content of coal concentrates and petroleum coke have been studied. The obtained data indicate an increase in the degree of orderliness of the coke structure and the appearance of a larger number of nanostructures when added to coal charges as an additive of petroleum coke in the amount of 5%. Also, a similar modification of the charge leads to an increase in gross coke output by 1.3-1.4%; an increase in the total sulfur content in coke by 0.12-0.14%; reduction of coke ash content by 0.3-0.4%; deterioration of mechanical <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(P_{25}$</tex> -by 0.2-0.5%; I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>- by 0.1-0.2%) and strength after reaction (CSR - by 0.6-0.8%), reactivity (CRI - by 0.2-0.3%) of coke, as well as structural strength (SS by 0.6-0.8%), abrasive hardness (AH by 0.6-1.1 mg) and specific electrical resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\rho$</tex> by 0.002-0.007 Ohm×cm). Due to the positive influence of the coal of the “Svyato-Varvarynska” coal processing plant on the quality indicators of the blast furnace coke, an improvement in the quality of the coke obtained with a greater share of it in the charge is observed. On the other hand, when using a coal charge characterized by the lowest content of the mentioned coal, the quality of the obtained coke decreases sharply.

articleTitle: Coke Electrical Resistivity as Cumulative Characteristic of its Properties
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The dependence of the resistivity of coke on the component composition of coal batches and the final temperature of the process was studied. Taking into account that the resistivity and reactivity are influenced by some common factors, such as temperature level and coke readiness, which indicates the orderliness of its structure, the relationship between these indicators was established. Electrical resistivity is a cumulative indicator of coke properties, the values of which are determined by ash content, sulfur content, volatile yield, petrographic composition and carbonization conditions of coal raw materials. The obtained mathematical dependencies are characterized by high correlation values (0.6-0.84). The proposed regression equations can be recommended for the optimization of the composition and quality of production batches, since they have a significant impact on the resistivity of coke. This is particularly relevant when coke is used in electrothermal processes, since the productivity, electrical and thermal efficiency of the furnace depend on the electrical resistivity of the coke.

articleTitle: Using Nanocomposite Materials to Strengthen Cylindrical Panels with Complex Base
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: This paper presents a brief overview of the research results on the effect of carbon nanotube reinforcement in functionally graded composites on the natural frequencies of cylindrical panels with a complex base. The modes of buckling for such panels under longitudinal and radial loading are demonstrated. The critical pressure values under such loading conditions are obtained. The research is conducted for five types of nanocomposites, which model one uniform and four gradient distributions of carbon nanotubes through the thickness of thin-walled structures. A mathematical model of the free vibrations of a nanocomposite cylindrical panel with a complex base in the form of two symmetrical rectangular cutouts on the sides is proposed. The case of a clamped panel is considered. The mathematical model is based on the use of the Rayleigh-Ritz method, the description of the displacement vector components based on Reddy's higher-order theory, and the application of the R-function method to describe the contour with rectangular cutouts on the cylindrical panel sides. The obtained results are can be used for studying the vibrations of nanocomposite cylindrical panels with a complex base under longitudinal and radial loading.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Investigation of W/Mg2Si Multilayer X-Ray Mirrors for the 0.9-2.5 nm and 25–35 nm Wavelength Ranges
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: This study investigates the fabrication and properties of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{W}/\mathbf{Mg_{2}}\mathbf{Si}$</tex> multilayer X-ray mirrors (MXMs) using DC magnetron sputtering. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{W}/\mathbf{Mg_{2}}\mathbf{Si}$</tex> MXMs with a period of about 3 nm were grown and characterised by X-ray reflectivity (XRR) and electron microscopy. The interlayer boundaries exhibited a roughness of ~0.3 nm, suitable for mirrors with such fine periods. During fabrication, interlayer interactions resulted in formation of a mixed zone at the Mg2Si-on-W interface within the tungsten layer. The composition of this mixed zone varied with layer thickness. Experimental XRR patterns showed mixed zone densities of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{16.1}\mathbf{g}/\mathbf{cm^{3}}$</tex> for a period of 3.1 nm and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{3.2}\mathbf{g}/\mathbf{cm^{3}}$</tex> for a period of 14.2 nm. Reflectivity measurements at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{Mg}-\mathbf{K}\boldsymbol{\alpha}$</tex> (9.89 nm) showed that the unoptimised <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{W}/\mathbf{Mg_{2}}$</tex> Si MXM performed comparably to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{W}/\mathbf{B}_{4}\mathbf{C}$</tex> MXMs, with a 5% advantage at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{Na}-\mathbf{K}\boldsymbol{\alpha}$</tex> (1.191 nm). These results highlight the potential of short period <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{W}/\mathbf{Mg2}$</tex> Si MXMs in X-ray spectral analysis for the detection of elements such as Mg, Na, F and O.

articleTitle: Alginate/Gelatin/Hydroxyapatite Porous Electrically Conductive Osteoplastic Biomaterial
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The process of the bone healing is a complicated and staged mechanism. The search for materials to optimize the bone healing is an important medical and social problem nowadays. Our aim was to create an osteoplastic material, which is an alginate-gelatin matrix cross-linked with divalent Ca, Zn, Cuions with immobilized particles <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\leq 163\mu \mathrm{m})$</tex> of nanostructured hydroxyapatite (HA) synthesized in the presence of cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB), a pore-forming agent, and with the addition of the organic conductive reagent polyaniline (PANI). It has been shown that the created biomaterials have a porous structure, and the degree of porosity depends on the component composition and shape of the biomaterial. Beads that contain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ca}^{2+}, \text{Zn}^{2+}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Cu}^{2+}$</tex> ions have porosity of about 17, 25 and 39%, and plates have porosity of about 30, 37 and 42%, respectively. The degree of swelling after 24 hours for HA/Ca/PANI, HA/Zn/PANI, HA/Cu/PANI samples was 424.8, 443.6, 432.4%, respectively, which satisfies their use as an osteoplastic material. The addition of PANI slightly reduces the porosity of samples that contain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Zn}^{2+}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Cu}^{2+}$</tex>, but at the same time increases their electrical conductivity by a factor of two compared to PANI-free samples. The electrical conductivity of the HA/Ca/PANI, HA/Zn/PANI, and HA/Cu/PANI samples is 1.319±0.032, 1.399±0.096, and 0.652±0.005 S/m, respectively. The synthesized osteoplastic material is promising for use in biomedical practice after clinical testing.
