articleTitle: Running Wave Interferometer with Active Medium
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The passive mode of operation of the running wave interferometer, which contains an active medium, is considered in detail in the work with the help of an analytical mathematical model. First, the working principle and mathematical model of the interferometer are described. The influence of the interferometer parameters on the duration of the transient process and on the value of the steady-state intensity of the output signal was studied. At the end, the features of the active mode of operation of the interferometer are briefly given.

articleTitle: The Magnitude and Shape of the Commutating Voltage of a Three-Phase Two-Bridge Compensating Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The results of a study of the process of formation of commutating voltage in a three-phase two-bridge compensation converter are presented. The converter under study is a representative of a new generation of devices of this type. It uses a new technical solution in terms of implementing a commutating link consisting of a three-phase capacitor battery and a three-phase group of fully controlled devices (for example, IGBT). In this case, the effect of controllability of the process of recharging the capacitors of the commutating link is achieved and conditions are created for changing the commutating voltage both in magnitude and in shape. The previous generation of compensation converters did not have this capability. New properties of the new generation converter make it possible to ensure the adjustability of its energy process.

articleTitle: Detection of Cardiac Arrhythmias Using Neural Network-Based Heart Rate Variability Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The paper discusses the application of neural networks for processing heart rate variability signals, which is necessary for more reliable diagnosis of cardiovascular diseases. The relevance of this task is due to the fact that computerized electrocardiogram processing systems, including neural networks, have firmly entered the practice of clinical research. The paper proposes, with the aim of increasing the reliability of diagnosis, to perform preprocessing of rhythmograms and to calculate a series of integral characteristics of cardiointervalograms using statistical and geometric methods. To solve the problem of diagnosing cardiac arrhythmias, a multilayer perceptron classifier of the form 11-10-4 was created. Preprocessing was performed to form input parameters, including the extraction of peaks and the formation of rhythmograms, as well as the calculation of heart rate variability parameters. The neural network receives 11 values for each ECG (electrocardiogram) signal as input: SDNN, SDANN, SDNNi, SDSD, NN50, pNN50, CV, Mo, AMo, VR, IN. Based on the ECG analysis results, it was classified into one of four classes: normal rhythm, atrial fibrillation, other types of arrhythmias, noise. Two algorithms were used for training: backpropagation and conjugate gradients. Testing the network on real ECGs showed a sufficiently high diagnostic accuracy (sensitivity not less than 85%, specificity 82%). The results of the work can be applied in automated ECG analysis systems, particularly in Holter monitors.

articleTitle: Study of Structural Properties of Cadmium Telluride Films Obtained on Different Substrates
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: Using modernized vacuum systems, it has been prepared a series of CdTe thin film samples by application of thermal vacuum evaporation method on three types of substrate material in order to investigate the varying of thin films structural parameters in dependence of material of substrate. The structural parameters were investigated by using the method of X-ray diffractometric analysis, based on which the lattice parameters, the sizes of the coherent scattering regions and the texture coefficient of the samples were obtained. According to the experimental study it was found that for samples obtained on dielectric substrate only the cubic phase of CdTe was spotted. In case of samples prepared on substrate with conductive layer it was spotted the two types of hexagonal phases and a presence a little quantity of cubic phase. Samples prepared on metal substrate contains practically only from the cubic phase of CdTe which can be connected with technological regimes of film samples obtaining. For this samples were spotted the value of lattice parameter which maximally close to the etalon value among all investigated samples which is also mainly connected with technological features, especially the speed of thin film growth.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Parameters of a Soft Switching DC/DC Converter with a Modified Push-Pull Current Source Inverter Stage for Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The article provides an assessment of the parameters of the power part of a DC/DC converter for transferring solar panel energy to a constant voltage network with the possibility of supporting the MPPT option. The primary stage has the push-pull topology of a current source inverter with an additional switch. The secondary stage is a half-bridge voltage source inverter. A special switching algorithm of separated commutation is described. It provides snubber turning-on of the current source inverter's switches and their natural turning-off in the mode of zero currents. The role of the non-dissipative turn-on snubber is performed by the leakage inductance of the matching transformer. For voltage source inverter MOSFETs the turning-on is natural in the mode of zero voltage. The role of the non-dissipative turn-on snubber may perform the own MOSFET's output capacance. Switches types were selected and static losses were estimated. Simulation confirmed the theoretical conclusions and the presence of soft switching modes of convertor's switches.

articleTitle: Electronic Parts to Design Colour Measurements Device for Analytical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: This article analyses colour sensor IC to construct colorimeter for analytical applications. A colour change is important marker in many chemical reactions it is usable in quantitative analysis of different compounds that is briefly discussed. Aim of the article compare colour sensor ICs for high integrated solution from market, discuss troubleshoots in the colorimeter construction with high resolution features. Proposed structure an analytical device adopted to work with different samples.

articleTitle: Analysis of Trade-Offs Between Accuracy And Speed of Real-Time Object Detectors for the Tasks of Explosive Ordnance Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: This paper investigates the performance trade-offs between accuracy and inference time in real-time object detection models, particularly for detecting landmines and unexploded ordnance (UXO). Using subsets from the COCO validation dataset, the models' performance is evaluated across various input resolutions. Object detection has seen substantial advancements over the past few decades, propelled by deep learning and enhanced computational resources. However, the balance between accuracy and inference time differs among models and configurations, requiring detailed evaluation to identify the optimal solution for specific applications like landmine and UXO detection. This balance is critical for autonomous robotic systems, where swift and accurate decision-making is imperative.

articleTitle: Study of the Architectural Features of the ResNet Neural Network Model for Solving the Task of Speaker Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The relevance of the use of speech recognition methods is due to the growing need for security, convenience, personalisation, efficiency and automation of business processes in various aspects of modern life. The authors can also mention the most modern factor that further increases the relevance of the study of speaker recognition methods protection against falsification and transcription of voice messages in social and communication platforms. The relevance of the identification and verification problem determines the variety of methods used to solve the problem from characteristics determined by the physical nature of sound to neural network models of deep learning. Considering the problem area and the subject of the study, the authors managed to offer a detailed systematization of speaker identification and verification approaches. As a result of the study, a generalized speaker recognition model based on the ResNet neural network model with convolutional architecture was proposed, for experimental testing of which a training dataset based on speeches of five speakers was prepared and restructured. Analysis of the model components revealed the possibility of improvement by accelerating the Fast Fourier Transform on a massively parallel computing system. This improvement showed the possibility of speeding up computations by up to 1,469 times even for small audio files (22.881 MB), using the data parallelism available in modern discrete GPUs, as well as the features of the FFT algorithm. The analysis of the relevance and demand for the problem of identification and verification has led to the creation of a detailed systematisation of approaches to speaker identification and verification, which clearly visualises the methods of signal processing, their purpose and the nature of the data. The study of the architectural features of the ResNet neural network model with convolutional architecture for speaker recognition showed an accuracy of 0.9747, achieved after 14 epochs of model training. After the 14th epoch, the model stops learning, as evidenced by the increase in the value of validation losses. The further development of the work is an in-depth analysis of speaker identification, namely, improving the model by the criterion of resistance to various speech characteristics, such as different accents, intonations, speech styles, etc. For this purpose, it is planned to revise the training set and expand it with different noise levels and different types of environment to assess the model's resistance to external factors.

articleTitle: Method of Detection of Intrusions Based on Stacking Meta-Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: An analysis of modern computer network intrusion detection systems was carried out. The application of machine and deep learning methods for classification problems has been investigated. The UNSW-NB15 dataset, developed at the Australian Cyber Security Center's (ACCS) Cyber Range Laboratory, contains data on normal network operations and synthetic intrusions. Data pre-processing was performed, including class balancing using the SMOTEENN method and selection of informative features using the Recursive Feature Elimination method. The possibility of using the stacking meta-algorithm to detect intrusions into computer networks has been investigated. A new algorithm for generating packets of raw data is proposed, which generates two sets of training data: one for training basic models, the other for a meta-model. A study of the effectiveness of using Random Forest, ANN, K Nearest Neighbor methods and Support Vector Machine and Random Forest as a decision-making meta-model was conducted. The use of the stacking meta-algorithm with the proposed algorithm for forming packets of output data, as well as basic models and a meta-model, led to a significant improvement in the quality of the model. It was found that, on average, recall and f1 score increased by 55.6% and 37.4%, respectively, compared to raw data and other models.

articleTitle: Methods and Means of Increasing the Accuracy of Assessment Technological Losses of Electricity in Distribution Overhead Power Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The article describes an innovative approach to calculating energy losses in distribution networks. The approach is based on the use of a device proposed by the authors, designed for operation in 6–10 kV networks with an isolated neutral. The device must be installed on all branches of the overhead power line and by measuring the current and temperature of the conductor, calculate the losses in the wire in p.u. By further multiplying the value of losses calculated by the device by the resistance of the line section, you can find the correct losses in the section. It is proposed to refine the method for calculating losses by the device by taking into account various factors: measurement of wire temperature, non-sinusoidal current, elongation of the conductor under the tension force, corrosion of the conductor over time. The calculation method that takes into account these factors is described in the work. Based on the obtained relationships, it is shown that the energy losses can be 1.28 times greater than those expected for a sinusoidal current with an increase in Total Harmonic Current Distortion from 0 to 50% and when the temperature changes from -40 to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+70^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>, the losses can vary from -24 to +17%.

articleTitle: Properties of Resonant Converter as Controlled Object With Amplitude, Frequency and Pulse-Width Methods of Output Voltage Regulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: On the basis of linearized mathematical models, an analysis of the dynamic and static properties of a two-bridge resonant converter with a series resonant circuit with amplitude, frequency, and pulse-width regulation methods was carried out from a qualitative point of view.

articleTitle: Selection of BESS Management Strategy and Capacity for Prosumer Microgrid Revenue
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: Due to the instability of renewable energy sources, it is difficult to maintain the sustainable operation of microgrids. Energy storage systems help to provide uninterrupted power supply to microgrids, but their integration faces the difficult task of determining the optimal parameters of energy storage systems. This study proposes a methodology for determining the optimal capacity of the energy storage system, taking into account various scenarios of the prosumer's microgrid operation to obtain maximum profit from working with the power grid. Two radically different scenarios for the operation of the prosumer's microgrid with the general power grid are considered. Where the scenarios are aimed at revenue from the maximum use of the solar generation system or the balanced use of all elements of the system. The paper considers a microgrid, on the example of a prosumer, which includes solar photovoltaic generation, a load profile, electricity storage systems and is connected to the power grid at a three-zone time of use tariff. To assess the effectiveness of these strategies, the analysis is carried out for two days for the winter season.

articleTitle: Business Process Control-Flow Complexity Prediction Using Machine Learning-based Tool
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: Business processes are structured sequences of activities, events, and other elements designed to fulfill customer needs in services or goods. Business process management is an approach used to combine information technology and management fields to develop, maintain, and improve organizational workflows. Business process modeling is a key technique employed for graphical description and analysis of organizational activities, it helps to understand, capture, analyze, and improve enterprise business processes. Thus, the quality of designed models should be carefully controlled to ensure timely business process modeling errors detection and prevention prior to they turn into errors leading to extra costs or other negative impacts on an organization. Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN) is the de-facto standard of workflow description in recent years, providing a well-structured notation to describe complex organizational activities. Hence, in this study we consider the complexity of BPMN models as one of the main quality attributes formulated in the business process modeling field. The task of complexity evaluation of BPMN models is addressed, the key complexity metrics of BPMN models are considered, a prediction machine learning model is proposed using linear regression model, the respective software tool is designed, implemented and verified. Obtained experimental results are analyzed and discussed.

articleTitle: Optimization of Neural Network Calculations Using Integer Arithmetic
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: Most of the sensor devices in the Internet of Things systems are based on energy-efficient microcontrollers, the computing resources of which are limited, as well as the amount of available memory. Increasing the security of the use of such devices with the help of neural networks is an important and urgent problem. The article describes the possibility of using artificial neural networks in small microcontrollers with limited resources. The purpose of this work is to check the possibility of calculating neural networks based on integer arithmetic to reduce the time of calculating a neural network and eliminate data normalization operations, as well as to evaluate the feasibility of using such neural networks in the field of security of the Internet of Things in comparison with traditional methods, such as black lists and white lists. The following results were obtained: when switching to integer arithmetic, compared to floating point, the accuracy of the result calculations is within the permissible error of neural network training, that is, it has not changed. Execution time decreased by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30-96 \%$</tex>, depending on the architecture of the microcontroller. The program size is reduced by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$22-48 \%$</tex>, also depending on the microcontroller architecture. Conclusions: the possibility and expediency of using neural networks optimized for microcontrollers with limited resources was proved. This will increase the security of Internet of Things systems, especially against device authentication threats and intrusion detection. Prospects for further research are determined.

articleTitle: Asymptotic Analysis of Nonlinear Modes of Multi-Walled Nanotubes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: Sanders-Koiter nonlinear shell theory is applied to obtain the partial differential equations, which describe the nanotube nonlinear oscillations. Three groups of nonlinearities are taken into account: the geometrical nonlinearity, Van der Waals nonlinearity and boundary condition nonlinearity. Using the weight residual method, the partial differential equations are transformed into the nonlinear ordinary differential equations, which have several internal resonances. The multiple-mode manifolds are applied to study nonlinear oscillations. Due to these manifolds, the finite degree of freedom nonlinear mechanical system is reduced into two degree of freedom system, which is analyzed by the asymptotic approach. The data of numerical analysis is presented on backbone curves.

articleTitle: Wetting of Polylactic Acid Solution Blow Spinning Nonwoven Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: Nanofibers have a wide range of applications due to their unique properties, and there are several methods to produce them to improve scalability and reduce production costs. The popular electrospinning technology has limitations in terms of low productivity and specific equipment. Solution blow spinning is a simpler and less expensive alternative that uses pressurized gas to form fibers, allowing for easier scalability and control of production speed. This study focuses on the wettability characteristics of polylactic acid (PLA)-based materials produced by solution blow spinning. PLA nanofibers were prepared using dichloromethane as a solvent. Scanning electron microscopy and contact angle measurements were used to analyze the surface topography and wetting properties. The wetting properties were analyzed using the Zisman plot technique. The results showed that low density samples (2 g/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) had an average fiber thickness of 200 nm and high-density samples (10 g/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) had an average fiber thickness of 400 nm. The water contact angles were 136° for the low-density samples and 130° for the high-density samples, indicating different degrees of hydrophobicity. Analysis of the Zisman plot showed that the high-density material exhibited greater stability in the Cassi state compared to the low-density materials. This study highlights the potential of solution blow spinning to produce PLA nanofibers for various applications, including biomaterials and wearable electronics.

articleTitle: Analysis of CT Parameters of Trabecular Tissue Density of Vertebral Body
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: This paper discusses the issues of analysis of trabecular bone density based on histology, CT and micro-CT imaging techniques. Trabecular bone volume was evaluated and compared for these imaging techniques based on the analysis of open access tomographic images. Statistical evaluation of segmentation thresholds was tested using the Otsu method

articleTitle: Optimization Methods and Transfer Learning for Brain Tumor Detection Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: This research analyzes methods for optimizing the training of convolutional neural networks, the features of using small datasets, and the use of Transfer Learning techniques to improve image recognition accuracy. The results of training these models were compared with each other on a test dataset for recognizing brain tumor in CT images.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Method for Recognizing Real and Generated Ukrainian-Language Voices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The modern development of speech synthesis technologies and convolutional neural networks (CNN) creates new opportunities and challenges in the field of voice recognition. One of the key tasks is to ensure the security and authenticity of audio information, especially in the context of information warfare and disinformation campaigns. In this context, the ability to recognize and identify generated voices becomes particularly important. This study aims to develop an intelligent method for recognizing real and generated Ukrainian-language voices using convolutional neural networks. The proposed method is based on the careful collection and preparation of data, the development and training of a CNN model, and its validation on test samples. Special attention is paid to ensuring the balance of the dataset, which is crucial for preventing model bias and improving its ability to generalize to unknown data. The model shows high performance in detecting real and generated voices, making this approach useful for local applications, particularly in Ukraine.

articleTitle: Kinetics and Degree of Swelling of Hemostatic Hydrogels with a Gelatin-Alginate System Modified with Humic Acids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: In this work, hemostatic hydrogels with a gelatin-alginate system modified to prevent wound infection by humic acids in aqueous solutions containing sodium and calcium ions were developed. It has been shown that by changing the type and concentration of humic acids containing sodium or calcium ions in a gelatin-alginate hydrogel, it is possible to regulate the equilibrium degree of swelling in the range of 2.1-13.6% and the swelling time of the gel in the range of 16–30 s at a rate absorption of liquid by gel located on the human body in the range of 0.87 - 1.15 ml/(s cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), The high rate of water absorption and ability to swell at physiological temperature have been experimentally confirmed, simulating the ability of gel dressings to quickly absorb blood and wound exudate to ensure hemostasis.

articleTitle: Justification Of The Calculation Of The Dynamic Characteristics Of Porlarized Monostable Electromagnets For Vacuum Switching Devices Using The Combined Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The paper considers the combined method of calculating the dynamic characteristics of a polarized electromagnet, which is used as a drive in vacuum contactors and medium voltage vacuum circuit breakers. The design of a monostable polarized electromagnet and the peculiarities of its operation during the switching on and off are considered. A calculation femm model of an electromagnet in a cylindrical coordinate system has been developed. The theoretical substantiation of the improved combined method of calculating the dynamic characteristics of an axially symmetric monostable polarized electromagnet, which is based on the numerical solution of the static equations of the electromagnetic field by the finite element method and the numerical solution of the transient equations of a nonlinear electric circuit, a magnetic circuit taking into account eddy currents, and nonlinear equations of motion is carried out. The developed combined calculation method allows to determine the current in the winding, the displacements and speed of the armature, the dependence of the armature pressing force to the stationary part of the magnetic core on the time of powering the coil winding during the operation of switching on the electromagnet, which is a necessary condition for designing such devices.

articleTitle: Challenges of Tracking Motor Disorders Using Smartphone-based Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: This paper describes the challenges of deploying neural network models on mobile devices for real-time body keypoint detection in medical and rehabilitation applications. Performance tests of these models were conducted, and the results were compared across different devices.

articleTitle: Nonstoichiometric Nickel Oxide Films Deposited by SILAR Method on Flexible Polyimide Substrates
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: In this work, nanostructured nonstoichiometric translucent nickel oxide films with a stable cubic rock-salt crystal structure and a predominant orientation along the <111> direction were obtained on polyimide substrates. Thanks to the cracks formed as a result of annealing these films at a temperature of 300°C for 3 hours in air, they can be used in flexible electronics as functional elements of resistive strain sensors.

articleTitle: Determining Dielectric Properties of Wood-Polymer Composite from Secondary Thermoplasts with Modified Wood Filler
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The article investigates the dielectric properties of wood-polymer composites. The purpose of the test is to determine the dielectric properties of wood-polymer composites based on secondary raw materials during their operation. Dielectric permeability, dielectric loss angle tangent, static charge and electrical resistance are investigated. The analysis of the experiments results showed that the investigated samples of the proposed wood-polymer composites, which are impregnated with a modifying mixture, which includes polystyrene foam, have better dielectric properties, which indicates the protection of the wooden filler from the acquisition of moisture during operation, and, accordingly, the preservation of operational characteristics. A description of the effect of acquired moisture on the wood-polymer composites operational characteristics is given.

articleTitle: Analysis of Entropy Indicators of Electromyographic Signals for Differential Diagnostics of Low Back Pain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: Low back pain is one of the leading causes of global years of living with a disability. Electromyography is one of methods used for the diagnostics of low back pain. Electromyographic signals are non-stationary. The theory of dynamical systems, also called chaos theory or nonlinear dynamics, can be used for processing of electromyographic signals. The concept of entropy is associated with the predictability of the values of the series and the entire system. Thus, it is of interest to conduct an extended study of entropy indicators of electromyographic signals from different diagnostic groups.

articleTitle: Improvement of the Model of Cylindrical Harmonics of the Magnetic Field of the Electromagnet of the Orientation Control System to Ensure Magnetic Compatibility of the Spacecraft
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: In the work, an analytical model of the external magnetic field of the electromagnet of the spacecraft orientation control system based on cylindrical harmonics was developed. Four different analytical models of the external magnetic field of the electromagnet with a cylindrical core were considered, and a comparative analysis with numerical calculation was conducted.

articleTitle: Biomechanical Analysis of Stress Fields in Atrophic Posterior Maxilla with Implant-Supported Cantilever Crown
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: Implant-supported cantilever crowns can serve as a viable alternative in certain clinical scenarios to circumvent additional surgical procedures either prior to or concurrently with implant placement. Despite the favorable clinical results seen with cantilever crowns, concerns have been raised regarding the long-term biomechanical implications and associated technical challenges. Multiple research investigations have demonstrated that implant-supported cantilever crowns have the potential to generate heightened stress concentrations within the underlying alveolar bone. The aim of the study is in the biomechanical analysis of stress fields in atrophic posterior maxilla with implant-supported cantilever crown. Functionally important two molars loss was analyzed to provide the implant placement in atrophic maxilla with types III and IV bone, when implantation is complicated due to insufficient bone height (less than 10 mm), low bone density and rigidity, thin cortical core (thickness less or equal to 0.5 mm). In such challenging conditions, placement of cantilever crowns was proposed as an advanced approach. The recommendations for practitioners were formulated after thorough modeling of bone-implant interface with preliminary evaluation of stress fields in adjacent bone. Two (narrow and wide) implants of two lengths were studied (4.5×5.0 mm, 4.5×8.0 mm, 6.0×5.0 mm, 6.0×8.0 mm) as the supports for two teeth loss restoration. Also, a wide spectrum of human bone elasticity parameters was studied in order to generalize the results of the study to wide range of patients (patient-specific approach). Validation of FEA algorithms was provided to receive necessary accuracy of numerical analysis and support developed clinical recommendations. Based on the conducted research results, we draw the attention of implantologists to the fact that the load-bearing capacity of proposed cantilever crown which are supported by short plateau implants is predetermined by the adjacent bone strains because bone stresses in all studied restorative structures were less than the bone ultimate strength.

articleTitle: Theoretical Foundations and Synthesis of Spinel-Type Ferrites Using the Nitrate-Citrate Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: Ferrites are a class of ceramic magnetic materials that have wide applications in electronics, telecommunications and magnetic recording. One of the effective methods for the complex ferrites synthesis is the nitrate-citrate method, which is based on the use of metal nitrates and citric acid for the formation of complex precursors, which after heat treatment form ferrites. The paper examines the principles of spinel-type ferrites compositions designing, which are based on information about the subsolidus state of phase-forming oxides. Based on the synthesis products phase composition prediction the rational compositions for the most energetically favorable conditions for cobalt and nickel ferrites obtaining have been determined. The results of the fine ferrite powders synthesis using the nitrate-citrate method and the prospects for their further use are also discussed.

articleTitle: Symbolic Regression-Based Models for Hyperelastic Material
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: Understanding and predicting material behavior is crucial for material design and optimization. Traditional phenomenological models, while simpler, often lack physical accuracy. Machine learning (ML) tools, such as symbolic regression (SR), offer a promising solution by generating human-readable mathematical expressions that fit given datasets. This study investigates the application of symbolic regression (SR) for modeling hyperelastic material behavior. We explore the effectiveness of an error metric based on implicit derivatives compared to the standard inverse normalized root mean squared error (NRMSE). Synthetic data generated from the Mooney-Rivlin model was used for training and evaluation. The results demonstrate that SR can capture the qualitative behavior of the material with moderate accuracy (R-squared values up to 0.86). The proposed implicit derivative metric (E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) did not consistently outperform the standard NRMSE metric (E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>). However, in specific cases (single hysteresis loop without constant search), E2 offered a visually better fit. The study highlights the challenges of defining suitable error metrics for SR in material behavior modeling. Further research is needed to refine the E2 metric and explore alternative approaches for improved accuracy and generalizability.

articleTitle: MSE Prediction in BPG-Based Lossy Compression of Grayscale Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: Visual information, such as images, is one of the most important parts of the digital realm. Its volume quickly increases due to better resolution of imagers and a large amount of images acquired each day. The acquired images should be stored on personal computers, servers, etc., and/or transferred via communication lines. A common way to reduce the data size is to apply compression techniques where lossy compression is often preferable because it is able to provide a significantly higher compression ratio compared to lossless compression. Meanwhile, it is necessary to control quality of lossy compressed images to avoid (minimize) negative consequences of introduced distortions. To solve this task, this paper proposes ways to predict mean squared error (MSE) of introduced distortions for better portable graphics (BPG) lossy compression. Such a prediction can be helpful in scenarios when an image has to be compressed in visually lossless manner or an appropriate compromise between the attained compression ratio (CR) and compressed image quality should be produced. It is shown that MSE is highly correlated not only with compression control parameter Q used in the BPG encoder, but with characteristics (complexity) of an image to be compressed. We present and compare several approaches to MSE prediction based on image fast preliminary analysis using local image activity and entropy. The practical recommendations for the MSE prediction are given.

articleTitle: Identification of Mathematical Model Parameters of Control Object by S-Shaped Acceleration Curve
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The identification of mathematical models of control objects and the calculation of their parameters according to the s-shaped acceleration curve, which is an integral part of the automatic control systems tunning, were considered. Most of the publications consider complex and cumbersome methods of parameter identification that are difficult to apply in practice. The peculiarities of control objects with a delay and mathematical models approximating such objects were considered. Such models are inertial links of the first and second orders with a delay. Using a specific example, four graphical-analytical methods for identifying parameters were analyzed and recommendations for their use were given. Attention was also focused on the possibilities and advantages of using the modern powerful MatLab software, which allows identifying the parameters of an object approximated by an inertial link of any order, which gives a fairly accurate result.

articleTitle: The Active Power of an Induction Generator with a Single Excitation Capacitor at Different Ways of the Load Switching
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: At present it's known about autonomous induction generator excitation by using three capacitors. In the article the results of experimental research on induction generator excitation by using a single capacitor have been considered. The article considers various methods of connecting the load to the induction generator stator winding terminals. The dependences of the active power generated by the induction generator on the rotor speed and the load current, for different values of the excitation capacitor capacitance have been obtained. Conclusions about the more preferable connection of a single excitation capacitor and the load when using a single excitation capacitor have been made.

articleTitle: Ternary Compounds of the $\text{BaO}-\text{Al}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{3}-\text{SiO}_{2}$ System and Heterogeneous Dielectrics Based on Them
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The results of study the samples material for the synthesis of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{BaAl}_{2} \text{SiO}_{6}$</tex> have determined a stepwise reaction mechanism of the phase composition formation. This mechanism is taking place through the primary formation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{BaAl}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{4}$</tex> with a corresponding shift in the stoichiometric ratio of the mixture ingredients and the accompanying synthesis of celsian <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{BaAl}_{2} \text{Si}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{8}$</tex>, which interact with each other during ongoing firing to obtain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{BaAl}_{2} \text{SiO}_{6}$</tex>. Given circumstances are important for predicting the properties and performance characteristics of heterophase materials in the case of obtaining the dielectrics based on the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{BaO}-\text{Al}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{3}-\text{SiO}_{2}$</tex> system. In particular, at synthesis of celsian ceramics is rational to have an overage of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiO}_{2}$</tex> in the raw mixtures, since in the case of an overage of BaO and/or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Al}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{BaAl}_{2} \text{SiO}_{6}$</tex> formation is expected, as shown in the corresponding reaction. Technological regulation of the ratio between crystalline phases in such materials will ensure their operational reliability under the complex influence of high-voltage pulses and temperature shocks.

articleTitle: Experimental Studies of Effectiveness of Combined Electromagnetic Silence of Power Lines Magnetic Fields
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: Purpose of work is combined electromagnetic silence effectiveness experimental studies including active and solid passive parts of overhead power lines magnetic field. Combined silence consists of double-circuit active and U-shaped solid passive part, and characterized by increased efficiency. Combined silence design problem reduced to geometric inverse magneto-quasi-static problem solution. Vector objective function of minimax vector optimization problem calculated based on three-dimensional Maxwell equations solution by COMSOL Multiphysics ® software package. Minimax vector optimization problem solution calculated based on multi-swarm particle optimization algorithm. Global optimum calculated from Pareto-optimal solutions taking into account binary preference relations. During combined silence design active silence system two compensation windings spatial location coordinates and compensation windings currents and phases calculated. The U-shaped solid passive silence parameters also calculated. Designed combined silence effectiveness based on three-dimensional modeling theoretical and experimental studies carried out.

articleTitle: Location Optimization of 3D Printing Filament in the Waveguide to Decrease Mismatch Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The 3D printing filament non destructive testing and measurement of parameters can be carried out using microwave devices at the microwave frequency range. As it is known, vector network analyzers for measurement parameters can be replaced by cheaper devices, scalar network analyzers or six-port reflectometers, one of them is a multiprobe microwave multimeter. The optimization of filament location in the multiprobe microwave multimeter is considered in the report. The location of filament that leads to mismatch uncertainty decreasing is in the circular polarization plane of rectangular waveguide.

articleTitle: Aspects of Microscopic Slides Automated Image Processing in Cytogenetic Analysis of Radiotherapy Effects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: This paper considers the main stages of automated processing of digital images of micropreparations for chromosomal analysis. The structure of the modern biomedical digital microscopy system is also proposed. The methods of processing and analyzing images of cytological micropreparations were tested. Conclusions were made regarding the diagnostic significance and informativeness of cytohistological research methods, and requirements for digital microscopy systems and prospects for their improvement were determined.

articleTitle: Robot Manipulator Optimal Control via Ring-Rot-PSO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: An optimal control problem of a 2-DOF robot manipulator is stated. The problem requires a transition of a manipulated body from an initial to a final position with a complex criterion minimization. It includes integral and maximal components, both involve robot power functions. The problem is reduced to a minimization of the nonlinear objective function of eight arguments. Its solution is found with Ring-Rot-PSO algorithm. Analysis of the optimal control shows the smoothness of robot links' movement and a significant decrease in undesired robot manipulator dynamic and energy indicators.

articleTitle: The Markov Model of Free Space Optical Network Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: Based on the analyses conducted in the article a simplified model of the monitoring system for optical networks in free space was developed. A method for monitoring transmitted and received optical signals was provided considering the operational principles of its components. Utilizing the proposed model matrices were constructed to reflect the ergodic chain regularities for establishing transition matrices based on Markov chains. Transition probabilities were calculated to ensure the stable operation of the monitoring system and corresponding graphs were constructed.

articleTitle: Control of Electric Drive for Inertially Stabilized Platform in Tracking Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: This paper deals with the research of control in tracking modes in inertially stabilized platforms assigned for a payload of moving objects. Features of tracking mode are described. Basic controls used in inertially stabilized platforms with tracking mode only are proposed. Different ways to organize feedback are given. Simulation of proposed control laws based on the example of tracking the position of the line-of-sight for observation device assigned for operation on the ground moving object including reaction on the step and sinusoidal signals have been carried out.

articleTitle: Nanoparticle and Polyaniline Loaded Neuroconduits: Electrical and Biological Properties
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: Nerve conduits based on natural Alginate (Alg) and Gelatine (Gel) polymers, doped with ZnO, Cu, and Ag nanoparticles (NPs), and electro conductive polymer Polyaniline (PANI) were synthesized. The introduction of ZnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">NPs</inf> and Ag<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">NPs</inf> led to an increase in electroconductivity from 0.04 mS/cm to 0.18 mS/cm (almost 5 times compared to the Control). At the same time, a slight increase in the electrical conductivity of the sample with Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">NPs</inf> was observed (up to 0.07mS/cm). PANI significantly increases electrical conductivity up to 1.8 mS/cm for its concentration of 0.5mg/ml. Introducing PANI to the neuro conduits granted electroconductivity. Being a conjugative polymer, PANI exhibits antioxidant activity (AOA). Cytotoxicity studies revealed that PANI - and ZnO-containing samples are non-toxic and suitable for medical use. However, AlgGelCu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">NPs</inf> and AlgGelAg<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">NPs</inf> in the applied concentration of the metal NPs exhibit moderate toxicity.

articleTitle: Software Development for Modeling Microstructures of Polycrystalline Materials by Cellular Automata Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: This paper deals with software package development for 3D modeling of material microstructures using the 3D cellular automata method (MatViz3D). The software package includes algorithms for modeling based on the Moore, von Neumann, radial, and probabilistic cellular automata models. It also includes a 3D scene construction module using OpenGL for visualizing microstructures, a program interface design module, and modules for calculating geometric twodimensional and three-dimensional characteristics of grains. Finally, the software package includes algorithms for comparing the obtained characteristics with experimental microstructures, using script graphs for this purpose. MatViz3D has been developed using the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{C}++$</tex> programming language and the OpenGL library. The program interface has been designed using the Qt framework. The algorithms for comparing the obtained characteristics with experimental microstructures have been implemented using the Python programming language and the Seaborn library.

articleTitle: Application of Transformers in Financial Analysis: Forecasting Stock Prices and Trading Volumes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The accurate forecasting of stock prices and trading volumes is critical for financial market participants, including investors, traders, and analysts. Traditional methods such as ARIMA and GARCH have been widely used, but they often struggle with capturing complex patterns in financial time series data. This paper explores the application of Transformer models, originally developed for natural language processing, in the domain of financial analysis. We provide a comprehensive overview of the Transformer architecture and its advantages over conventional models. Using historical stock market data, we build and train a Transformer model to predict future stock prices and trading volumes. Our results demonstrate that Transformers can effectively capture intricate temporal dependencies and deliver more accurate forecasts compared to traditional methods. The findings highlight the potential of Transformer models to enhance decision-making processes in financial markets. Future research directions and practical implications of implementing Transformers in real-world financial systems are also discussed.

articleTitle: Threshold Conditions for 1-D Model of Laser Cavity Covered with Noble Metal Film
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The threshold conditions for the natural modes of a solid-state laser model containing a flat-layered cavity of gain material are considered. The cavity is placed between a noble metal substrate and the same material superstrate film. We use the Lasing Eigenvalue Problem approach to find the mode-specific frequencies and the corresponding to them threshold gain index values. The results obtained clarify the effect of the noble metal film thickness on the lasing mode characteristics. This analysis can be used in the laser performance optimization.

articleTitle: Methodology for Creating Annotated Datasets of Biological Objects in Microscopic Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The study presents a methodology for automatically creating an annotated dataset for further use in training neural networks. The method is based on the Crisp-DM framework and consists of 6 stages: business understanding, data understanding, data preparation, modeling, evaluation, deployment, which has been modified due to the specifics of computer vision tasks. As a modeling method, the k-means method is proposed, which is applied to the normalized area and average color data of a given object. The approach is tested for creating an annotated dataset for recognizing and localizing cells of different types in blood smear images. The output is a dataframe with the columns file_name, xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax, type, area, which represent the file name, the coordinates of the upper left and lower right points of the bounding boxes, the cell type, and its area. Using these parameters and image processing libraries it is easy to add bounding boxes to the original images. The resulting annotated dataset is analyzed. Metrics were calculated and a loss matrix was constructed. All calculations were performed using the Python programming language and the Pandas, numpy, openCV, and matplotlib libraries.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of the Harmonic Distortion at Points of Common Coupling of Urban Substations in Ukraine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: Purpose of work is experimental study of nonsinusoidal current and voltage transformer substation loads of urban areas in Ukraine, research of harmonic structure of group loads and their compliance with international standards. Methods. The monitoring was held for a week at the input low voltage power transformer at urban transformer substation using RESURS-UF2M device. Results. Total harmonic distortion THD of voltage on tires 0.4 kV transformer substation does not exceed 8%. The level of individual harmonic voltage does not exceed 5%. Overnight TDD current value at input 0.4 kV transformers exceed twice the limit values according to the standard IEEE 519–2014 in phase B daily 4.4 percentile and slightly in phase C - 0.1 percentile. The results of the weekly monitoring are based on 10-minute averaged values, TDD current of all three phases exceeded the limit value (5%) in phase A - 38.9 percentile, phase B - 51.1 and phase C - 6.9. So there are violations of the standard requirements of weekly 95th percentile within 5% in all phases. In terms of individual harmonics during the week exceeding 95 percentile permissible values were recorded for 3 and 5 harmonic phases A and B, the value of which amounts to 7% of the maximum demand current at the point of common coupling (PCC). Exceeding the limit values was recorded, more than 30% of the time monitoring. This is does not correspond to standard IEEE 519–2014. Practical value. To control the level of higher harmonics in the PCC it is necessary to use the standard IEEE 519–2014. At locality substations with high harmonic currents, it is advisable to install HMTs transformers and harmonic active filters.

articleTitle: The Method of Dynamic Routing in Self-Healing Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The report proposes a dynamic routing method for Self-healing Networks (ShN). The method takes into account the specific features of ShN. During routing, the flow of service information is reduced. The search for the optimal route is carried out using a convolutional neural network. The method significantly outperforms existing methods when some network nodes fail.

articleTitle: Evaluation of MPPT Efficiency as a Function of PV Current Ripple
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The article presents an assessment of the reduction in maximum power extraction by solar panels as a function of pulsation. The typical current-voltage characteristic of solar panels is expressed using the polynomial approximation method. In the MatlablSimulink program, a model of a block of solar panels has been developed, the power of which is taken by a boost ds/ds converter with the MPPT function. The dependences of the value of the selected solar power as a function of the harmonic distortion coefficient of the panel current have been established.

articleTitle: Study of Amplitude-Frequency Characteristics of Biological Tissues
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The article examines the reaction of biological tissues based on the principle of measuring and analyzing signals in the frequency domain. It is shown that the shape of the frequency response can serve as an informative sign of the volumetric content of healthy cells in the studied volume of biological tissue and, therefore, can be a sign of its viability.

articleTitle: Special Properties of Composite Materials of Alkaline Earth Element Oxide Compounds
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: The paper presents the results of experimental studies of the electrophysical properties of composite materials based on aluminate and barium titanate oxide compounds. According to standard methods, samples of aluminate-titanate-barium cement were synthesized and studied, and its main parameters characterizing ferroelectric and piezoelectric materials were determined: dielectric constant, dielectric loss, electrical resistance, Curie point, and piezoelectric modulus. Of the known dual compounds formed in this system, barium aluminate (BaAl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>) and barium titanate (BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) are of considerable interest from the point of view of obtaining cements with enhanced electrophysical properties. The influence of the mineralogical composition of the cement under study on its electrophysical properties was investigated. It was determined that cements containing 60–95 wt. % of barium titanate. A rational cement composition was chosen - 5% BaAl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>+ 95% BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. Cements with a lower content of barium titanate are characterised by reduced ferroelectricity. The dielectric loss tangent of aluminate-titanate-barium cement increases with the increase in the content of barium aluminate. The cement's Curie point has been determined and is 120°C. The piezoelectric modulus of the cement samples under consideration is higher, the higher the content of barium titanate in the cement, which is a carrier of piezoelectric properties. The study makes it possible to effectively use composite materials based on oxide compounds of aluminate and barium titanate in the production of ferroelectric and piezoelectric ceramics.

articleTitle: Study of the Possibility of Placing the Transformer Underground in Compliance with the Thermal Regime
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: Placing transformers in underground bunkers will increase their security and make it harder to damage them, which will ensure stability in the power system against missile attacks on the power structure during hostilities. The purpose of this work was to increase the security of the power system by moving transformers to underground bunkers. As a result of the work, it was found that there are currently no reliable means of protecting transformers in Ukraine, so the main design parameters of the bunker for placing a transformer in it were determined, the required capacity of the ventilation system was determined, as well as the service life of the transformer at the proposed location. It was determined that with the proposed placement and cooling of the transformer in the bunker, the service life of the transformer is not reduced. To verify the adequacy of the mathematical models, identification was performed, which showed that the error was no more than 7%. We also performed calculations using the finite element method and compared the results with the results of calculations using the proposed formulas. The error was no more than 4%. The scientific novelty and practical value of the work is the first scientifically substantiated technical possibility of placing transformers underground without affecting the service life of the transformer itself. The obtained results and calculation methods can be used in practice. The mathematical models and formulas proposed in this paper are universal, so they are applicable to most power transformers.

articleTitle: Correlation of Thermal Mode with the Limit Electrical Load of High Voltage Carbon Resistors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: High-voltage impulse installations have found wide use within the scope of testing structures and equipment for the action of an electromagnetic field and electric discharges, as well as in the field of materials processing. One of the important elements of such installations are high-voltage resistors, which are used in the capacitor charge units, the forming unit, and also as the main elements of measuring voltage dividers. The purpose of this work is to determine the thermophysical characteristics of TVO-10 and TVO-60 resistors, taking into account the dependence of the heat transfer coefficient on the overheating of the resistor, as well as establishing the relationship between the thermal mode and the limit electrical loads of the resistors. Methods of experimental determination of heat capacity and heat transfer of volumetric elements, methods of integro-differential mathematical modeling, as well as a method of empirical confirmation of calculation results during the operation of resistors in the second and millisecond range of current flow were used. According to the results of resource tests of resistors, a method of electrothermal calculation of the optimal operating mode was proposed.

articleTitle: A Study on the Accuracy of Identification of the Oculo-Motor System based on Integral Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: Integral nonlinear models are used for modeling the human oculomotor system (OMS), accounting for both nonlinear and inertial properties. Experimental “input-output” data identify transient functions and their diagonal intersections of second and third orders. Eye-tracking technology records eye responses to visual stimuli at various horizontal distances from a starting position on a monitor screen. The research aims to evaluate OMS identification accuracy using eye-tracking data by assessing calculation errors of multidimensional transient functions with nonlinear dynamic identification methods based on Volterra series and polynomial models. The study focuses on nonparametric identification of the OMS using Volterra models in the time domain and on algorithmic and software tools for determining OMS dynamic characteristics from eye-tracking data, examining models obtained through the approximation method, compensation method and the least squares method (LSM). Nonlinear dynamic identification methods for the human OMS, based on Volterra series and polynomials, were implemented in Python. Accuracy estimates for various OMS models (linear, quadratic, and cubic) were derived from three response sets to test signals of different amplitudes. Identical models were obtained using the approximation method and the LSM for the same test signals. Error analysis showed that a second-degree polynomial model built using LSM based on three responses has twice the accuracy of similar models constructed from two response data sets. Thus, for further studies of the psychophysiological state based on nonlinear dynamic models of the OMS using three response data sets, a quadratic Volterra polynomial model is recommended.

articleTitle: Miniature Hybrid Quantum Optomechanical Sensors for Acceleration Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: A number of applications, particularly aerospace, require accurate, drift-free acceleration measurement with the help of miniature instruments. For such measurements, hybrid quantum optomechanical sensors are used, which provide both high speed measurements using the optomechanical part of the sensor and drift-free measurements that do not require additional calibrations using the quantum part of the sensor. It is proposed to make the quantum part of the sensor based on ensembles of negatively charged nitrogen vacancy (NV) in diamond. Configurations of optomechanical sensors and systems for creating a uniform microwave electromagnetic field applied to an ensemble of NV centers have been proposed. Using mathematical modeling, the effectiveness of the developed systems is shown.

articleTitle: Increasing the Heat Resistance and Reducing the Flammability of Reinforced Plastics Used for Electroengineering Purposes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 5th KhPI Week on Advanced Technology (KhPIWeek)
abstract: Investigations were carried out to study hot-curing epoxy polymer composite materials (PCM) and reinforced plastics based on them to increase their heat resistance, reduce their flammability and to establish the possibility of their use for electrical engineering. Structuring processes, a number of physical and mechanical properties, chemical resistance and atmospheric resistance of PCM and reinforced plastics, and also the electrical properties of materials depending on the chemical nature of hardeners and dispersed fillers in the composition of composite materials have been studied. It was established that the addition of certain hardeners to the composition of polymer compounds and the combination of epoxy compounds with some dispersed fillers enable the production of composite materials with new physicochemical, technological and operational properties. The developed PCM and reinforced plastics can be recommended for the manufacturing of the products used for electrotechnical purposes (insulators for high-voltage power lines, profiles for dry transformers, equipment elements for the structures with an increased risk of electric shock, etc.).

articleTitle: Theoretical Analysis of Peculiarities of Phase Formation of Ferromagnetics of CoO – BaO – Fe2O3 System

The choice of the studied system from the point of view of obtaining traditional ceramic ferrites on the basis of binary compounds of the system is justified, and the possibility of obtaining ferromagnetics on the basis of ternary oxides of the above system is shown. The results of calculation of the Gibbs free energy change with temperature for model reactions simulating all possible variants of synthesis and decomposition of ternary oxide compounds of the above system are presented.
